samples.summary: No test that a guard is *un*registered when `active` flips true→false or the guarded component unmounts
samples.evidence: The only "not guarded" case renders with `active={false}` from the start (`navigation-guard.test.tsx:105-112`), so `register`'s returned cleanup in `use-navigation-guard.ts:52-55` is never exercised. Nothing asserts that after a document finishes saving (mayHaveUnsent → false) or after the editor unmounts, the stale guard stops being asked. If that cleanup regressed, a stale closure would keep returning a prompt and every subsequent in-app navigation, app-wide, would pop "Leave without saving?" forever — a visible break the green suite would not catch. Neither sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx nor navigation-guard.test.tsx toggles `active` after mount.

samples.summary: The `pathOf`/`leaving` path comparison is only ever tested under `MemoryRouter` with no basename, while the app mounts the router with `VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME`
samples.evidence: `leaving()` compares `navigator.createHref(to)` against `navigator.createHref(locationRef.current)` (provider lines ~36 and ~100-106). Both tests render `<MemoryRouter initialEntries={['/s/doc-1']}>` with no `basename` (navigation-guard.test.tsx:58, sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx:~86), whereas App.tsx passes `basename={import.meta.env.VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME}`. `useLocation()` returns a basename-stripped pathname while `createHref` re-applies the basename, so a basename deployment exercises a code path no test covers: if the two sides ever resolve differently the guard silently never fires (edits lost) or fires on every same-page query update. No test sets a basename anywhere for this component.
searchedFor: both new test files read in full

verdict.reason: Verified directly: no test exercises the guard-unregistration path. In navigation-guard.test.tsx the sole "not guarded" case (:105-112) renders active={false} from mount, and neither Harness nor any test rerenders/toggles active or navigates again after the guarded Editor unmounts (:89-96 completes navigation before unmount, then asserts nothing further). sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx sets mockCtx once before render in every case; its "every change is on the server" case (:138-153) keeps mayHaveUnsent true and covers the fire-time decline path, not cleanup. The closest sibling coverage, sync-status-chip.test.tsx:145-168, asserts unloadGuards()===0 after a true→false flip, but that measures the separate beforeunload listener effect (sync-status-chip.tsx:92-103) with the chip rendered outside NavigationGuardProvider, so register is the no-op default context (use-navigation-guard.ts:29-31) and guardsRef.delete (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:83-85) is never involved. Repo-wide greps for useNavigationGuard/GuardRegistryContext and "Leave without saving" surface only those two test files plus the chip source — no e2e coverage. A regression in use-navigation-guard.ts:54-57's cleanup would leave a stale guard prompting on every subsequent in-app navigation app-wide, a user-visible break the green suite would not catch: major under the missing-tests lane.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `leaving()` compares `pathOf(base, to)` with `pathOf(base, locationRef.current)`, both via `navigator.createHref` (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:40-42, 99-102), and the docstring at lines 36-38 asserts the basename resolves identically on both sides. The app mounts the router with a configurable basename (App.tsx:95; VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME is a documented deployment knob per .env.production.example:46 and self-hosting.md:381). A case-insensitive grep for `basename` across all of packages/frontend returns no test hits at all — only App.tsx, the provider comment, unrelated sheetImportBaseName helpers, and docs/comments. A repo-wide grep for NavigationGuardProvider/useNavigationGuard shows exactly two test files, and navigation-guard.test.tsx:58 renders `<MemoryRouter initialEntries={['/s/doc-1']}>` with no basename for every case, including the same-page-query case at lines 114-120. There is no e2e suite (`**/e2e/**` empty) and no shared harness injecting a basename. This is more than narrowed coverage: react-router prefixes the basename onto the `to` passed to navigator.push while useLocation() returns a stripped pathname, so the symmetry the comment claims is exactly the untested assumption; if it fails, a basename deployment either prompts on every same-page query rewrite or silently never fires and loses unsent edits. Dependencies are not installed in this tree, so I could not verify the router internals to show the gap is harmless — I therefore cannot name a refutation ground.
